title: Connect The Artist, Organisation And What I Found
objective: Use real experience records to explain what you found about an artist and an arts organisation, and check both are evidenced.

blocks.text: BUILD · Art · Trinity Arts Award Explore. Connect The Artist, Organisation And What I Found.
Objective: Use your real records. Say what you found about the artist and the arts group. Check that you have both.
Success evidence: Keep a finding from each real role. Show a link that the records support, or label your own comparison. Give each file and page. Name any work still to do.
You can explore through looking, listening, asking and trying. Choose a way to take part that works for you. You do not need to share private facts about your life.
We may go to them, they may come in, or we may meet live on screen. The route comes from the current slot card. No meeting is promised by this deck.
40-minute lesson frame. Staff may extend or split the real experience across sessions.

This deck serves Explore Part B, Explore. Part B requires at least one artist AND at least one arts organisation, through live or active experience. Desk research alone fails; archives and prerecorded video are preparation only. Explore has four parts, each a distinct activity. Overall Pass allows ONE Attempted. Any Not Attempted = Below Pass. The whole Explore portfolio has a 10-file cap, organised digitally by part. The three assessment areas are art form knowledge and understanding, creativity, and communication. Results are Pass or Below Pass only. Only an adviser trained at Explore may assess; delivery is through a validated centre. Neither local training nor validation is asserted as confirmed here. Advisers must not write plans, reviews or evidence for pupils. Scribe or record the pupil's own words and check them back unchanged. Core, Extend and Challenge are support routes within Explore and retain the live or active requirement. An evidence locator names the filename plus page, slide or timecode. Read the current PRACTITIONER_SLOT and ORG_SLOT from tools/artsaward/SLOTS.json; no candidate name or date is embedded here. R1 pupils visit, R2 the artist or arts organisation comes in, R3 live remote exchange: all remain unconfirmed until actually arranged. Do not treat a recorded video as a live exchange. Source: tools/artsaward/SPEC.json, Explore and universal rules. This deck consolidates Explore Part B only. It does not replace either required live/active element with a folder check or a classroom model. Use the actual artist and organisation records and check identities against the current slots. A single genuine experience can serve both if the pupil’s exploration of each is clear. If two experiences involved unrelated people and groups, allow a comparison of their arts roles without inventing a working relationship. Missing actual participation must be completed when arranged, with time beyond this lesson if needed. The pupil’s explanation is theirs; do not author it for them. Explaining Part B findings here is a formative learning check, not a claim that the distinct Explore Part D enjoyment/achievement share is complete.

stages.title: Arrival · retrieve
stages.data-ta1: Check the actual records before beginning. Do not infer completion from a filename, a finished worksheet or attendance at the lesson.

blocks.text: Bring the real records together
Find your artist record and arts group record. Put them where you can see both.
Look at each label. Does it show a real session, preparation or a job still to do?
A prepared question is useful, but it is not the reply. A group name is useful, but it does not show how you took part.
If a real element is missing, tell staff. Keep its space open on your sheet. You will need a real way to explore it when arranged.
If both records are ready, find something you learnt from each. Choose a detail you can show or explain in your own words.
Today you will connect those findings with care.

stages.title: Starter · create the need
stages.data-ta1: Make and place the paper form live. State that this is a classroom model, with no claimed organisation or outside artist contact.

blocks.text: Rehearsal: two roles in one small scene
Watch the adult fold a piece of paper so it stands. Then they place it where it can be seen from two seats.
Point to the making choice. Then point to the choice that helps someone see the work.
The fold and the display have different jobs. In this classroom model one adult did both.
A real artist and arts group may work together. They may also be quite separate. We need a record to tell us which is true.
Keep this model labelled rehearsal. It helps us talk about roles. It cannot take the place of exploring the real artist and group.

stages.title: I Do · model
stages.data-ta1: Model the method on visible classroom actions only, then guide the pupil to their own real records. An apparent shared theme does not establish employment, membership or collaboration.

blocks.text: Use the record before you make a link
Start with the artist record. Find the real name and the action you took part in. Look at the detail you chose to keep.
What did you find out about the person's art or way of working? Point to the part that supports your answer.
Now do the same for the arts group. Find its real name. Look for your action and what you found about its work.
Do the records show that the person and group worked together? Perhaps the source names a workshop the group ran with that artist. Check the source before you say so.
If the records do not show a working link, do not make one up. You can still compare what you explored.
The artist may have helped you notice a making choice. The group may have helped you notice how people can use or see art. Use only the details in your own records.
A link should help explain the work. It should not add a new fact just to make a neat story.
Keep a question mark where you need to find out more.

blocks.title: Build the connection from real records
blocks.caption: Open, find, explain and check the link.
blocks.alt: Four boxes lead from opening both records to finding a detail from each, explaining the findings and checking whether a proposed link is a fact or a comparison.

stages.title: We Do · everyone commits
stages.data-ta1: Suggested sort: A/C preparation; B/D can evidence real exploration if accurate and located. All examples are visible below. Check quality and context rather than automatically accepting a record type.

data.heading: What can this record tell us?
data.instruction: Sort these made-up cases. Some help us get ready. Others keep what someone did in a real session.

items.label: A logo copied before an activity.
items.feedback: A logo can help identify a group. It does not show your active exploration.

items.label: A true note of a real artist session. It keeps what the pupil asked and how they responded.
items.feedback: This can record artist exploration when it accurately names the session and action.

items.label: Notes made only from an old film of a workshop.
items.feedback: The film may help you prepare. It does not itself show your live or active exploration.

items.label: A true note from a real arts group session. It keeps what the pupil did and found out.
items.feedback: This can record arts group exploration when its source and the real action are clear.

data.discussion: Find a detail in each of your real records. If one is missing, name what still needs to happen. These made-up cards are not your own work.

stages.title: I Do 2 · connect
stages.data-ta1: Accept a comparison when no organisational relationship is evidenced. Do not supply facts to make the pupil’s connection more impressive.

blocks.text: A fact or your own comparison?
Here are two made-up notes for practice.
Artist note: I tried a fold the artist showed.
Group note: I moved a display so people could see the work.
We can compare two jobs. One helps to make art. The other helps people see it.
Can we say the artist works for that group? No. These notes do not show that.
A real source may name a workshop the group ran with that artist. Then we can say they worked together at that workshop. It still does not tell us the artist is on the staff.
Now look at your own two records. What can each one show?
If both name a real shared event, point to that source. If they do not, keep your link as a comparison.
Say what is alike or what differs. Do not add a fact to make a neat story.
Keep a real detail from each record beside your words. If you are unsure, keep a question to ask.

boxes.head: WORKING LINK
boxes.line2: name the record that supports it

boxes.head: MY COMPARISON
boxes.line1: I notice a shared idea or change
boxes.line2: no claim that they work together

blocks.title: Two different kinds of connection
blocks.caption: Say whether it is a real link or your comparison.
blocks.alt: The left panel needs source evidence for a working link. The right panel is the pupil’s comparison and does not claim the artist and group worked together.

stages.title: We Do 2 · lab
stages.data-ta1: Use a willing partner or staff support. Check locators and meaning. Where an actual element is ready to complete, support it with sufficient time and accurate capture; otherwise retain the next action.

blocks.text: Check the finding with someone
Show your chosen detail to a partner or staff member. Tell them which record it comes from.
Name the filename and page, slide or timecode. Ask them to find the detail. A quick point can help if reading is hard.
Now show the second record. Can they find that one too?
Explain your link or comparison. Ask if it is clear which parts are facts and which are your own thoughts.
If a real session is missing, tell staff. Choose the next real action together. A live activity can take place when it is properly arranged. A new invented note cannot fill that gap.

stages.title: Independent · evidence
stages.data-ta1: Scribe or record the pupil’s own meaning without improving it. All tiers retain both live/active elements; a supported explanation is not permission to omit one.

blocks.text: Make your own account of what you found
Use your real records to show what you found about both roles. You may write, draw, speak or use a short recording.
Name the artist and arts group accurately. Keep your own action in each experience clear.
Explain a detail from each. Then add your supported link, your comparison or the question you still have.
Keep each filename and page, slide or timecode beside the finding. The reader should be able to follow it back to the real moment.
If preparation is all you have for one element, say so. Keep that gap as a next action. Complete the real session when arranged.
Save this account with Part B. Keep the original records too.

items: Core · use prompts to find both real experience records. Point, speak or draw what you found about the artist and arts group. Keep the two findings and their file locations. If a live or active element is missing, name it as a next action.
Extend · explain both findings in your own layout. Use the records to show a true working link or make a clearly labelled comparison. Keep both live or active elements and exact locations.
Challenge · keep both real findings and records. Check a possible link in more than one piece of evidence. Explain what is known and what remains only a question. Do not turn a guess into a fact.

stages.title: Exit · Audience and Influence
stages.data-ta1: Record the true status of both elements and any next arrangement. Completion is checked against the requirement, not declared because this fourth Part B lesson has ended.

blocks.text: What is ready, and what is next?
Point to a finding you can now explain. Say which real record supports it.
Check both roles one last time. Is the artist explored through a real session? Is the arts group explored through a real session too?
Tell staff about any work still to do. Leave that status honest.
Keep the ideas you found interesting. They can help you choose new art to make later. These records stay a clear account of what happened in Part B.

checks: Both the artist and arts organisation are identified from real sources.
Each element has real live or active evidence, or is marked honestly as still to do.
The account gives my own action and finding for each role.
A working link is source-supported; a comparison is labelled as my own thought.
Both locations name a filename plus page, slide or timecode.
